discovery: Discovery of metal halide perovskites as highly efficient solution-processed photovoltaic semiconductors
motivation: Miyasaka first demonstrated (2009) that organolead halide perovskites act as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells. Park (2012) produced the first stable solid-state perovskite cell exceeding 9% efficiency, and Snaith (2012-2013) showed that perovskites are not merely sensitisers but ambipolar semiconductors with long carrier diffusion lengths, enabling planar thin-film devices. Together these discoveries revealed a new class of defect-tolerant semiconductors: low-temperature, solution-processed films whose sharp absorption edge, tunable bandgap and long carrier lifetimes rival those of single-crystal silicon. Certified efficiencies rose from 3.8% to over 26% within fifteen years, and perovskite-silicon tandems now exceed 34%, beyond the single-junction limit of silicon. The physics of these materials, from polaron screening to ion migration, has reshaped semiconductor science, while commercial modules are entering production. This is a discovery of genuine and growing use to humanity in the transition to clean energy.
